engine_interface.definition: Translates harmonic state mutations into elemental thermodynamic shifts.

electric_external.definition: Authored state marker for opposing microscopic processes continuing at equal rates with no net macroscopic change.
Authored state marker for chemical and electrical driving forces balanced with no net reaction current.
Authored state marker for an electrode potential at which an electrochemical reaction has no net forward or reverse rate.
Authored state marker for a system held at uniform or actively controlled constant temperature.
Authored state marker for a temperature difference yielding a Seebeck voltage while no current is drawn.
Authored state marker for coexisting phases with balanced chemical potentials, such as liquid and vapor at saturation.
Authored state marker for change slow enough to remain near equilibrium throughout a process.
Authored state marker for absorbed radiative power equal to emitted radiative power.
Authored state marker for the ideal limiting condition with no entropy production.
Authored state marker for heat generation, absorption, and outward rejection balancing so internal energy remains constant.
Authored state marker for constant macroscopic properties maintained by continuous energy, matter, or charge throughflow.
Authored transformation marker for reversible dielectric or ferroelectric temperature change caused by an applied-field change.
Authored transformation marker for expansion at constant temperature that converts absorbed heat into outward mechanical work.
Authored transformation marker for heat absorption or release during a phase transition while temperature remains nearly constant.
Authored transformation marker for current causing a junction to absorb heat at one side and reject it at the other.
Authored transformation marker for heat exported by a controlled melting, boiling, condensing, or freezing transition.
Authored transformation marker for surface temperature adjustment through balanced absorbed and emitted radiation.
Authored transformation marker for a temperature difference generating an outward electrical potential.
Authored transformation marker for sensing a thermal deviation and actively restoring a temperature set point.
Authored transformation marker for electrical work moving heat from a colder region to a hotter external sink.
Authored transformation marker for reversible heat absorption or evolution along a current-carrying conductor with a temperature gradient.
Authored transformation marker for threshold-controlled activation or deactivation of a heat-control pathway.
Authored transformation marker for changing temperature producing surface charge or current as an external electrical signal.
Authored structural marker for an idealized surface emitting the maximum possible thermal radiation for its temperature.
Authored structural marker for a two-phase transport structure carrying heat to an exterior radiating surface.
Authored structural marker for a surface or interface maintained at nearly constant temperature.
Authored structural marker for heat exchange through controlled melting, freezing, evaporation, or condensation.
Authored structural marker for a boundary between coexisting phases where latent heat can be absorbed or released.
Authored structural marker for an exterior surface whose temperature is set by radiative gains and losses.
Authored structural marker for the fluid region next to a surface where temperature changes from wall to bulk conditions.
Authored structural marker for a sensor, controller, and actuator arrangement maintaining a target thermal state.
Authored structural marker for an exterior surface designed to reject excess heat through infrared emission.
Authored structural marker for a high-conductance link carrying heat from a source to a controlled sink or radiator.
Authored structural marker for a junction of dissimilar conductors converting a temperature difference into voltage.
Authored structural marker for a semiconductor junction array used for Peltier cooling or Seebeck power generation.
Authored structural marker for series-connected thermocouples amplifying a thermal gradient into an outward electrical signal.
Authored structural marker for a circulating liquid-vapor system regulating temperature through latent-heat transport.
Authored transfer marker for heat moving through a solid path toward an external sink or radiator.
Authored transfer marker for heat carried outward by moving liquid or gas.
Authored transfer marker for field-controlled heat movement caused by reversible electrocaloric temperature change.
Authored transfer marker for heat or matter rejection to the environment that preserves local order or steady operation.
Authored transfer marker for heat exchange at constant temperature through a reservoir or phase transition.
Authored transfer marker for energy movement through a phase change rather than an ordinary temperature rise or fall.
Authored transfer marker for current-driven heat transport across a thermoelectric junction.
Authored transfer marker for a temperature change becoming an outward electrical output signal.
Authored transfer marker for net outward thermal-radiation emission to a cooler environment.
Authored transfer marker for a temperature difference converting into an observable electrical signal.
Authored transfer marker for bidirectional infrared energy transfer with net direction set by temperature and emissivity.
Authored transfer marker for heat-flow imbalance converting into exported electrical power.
Authored transfer marker for heat carried outward by evaporation and returned by condensation or liquid flow.

magnetic_internal.definition: State without net thermal, mechanical, or chemical driving forces.
Condition in which systems share a temperature and exhibit no net heat exchange.
Condition in which opposing chemical reactions balance.
Balance of forces and pressures with no net mechanical acceleration.
Balance of chemical potentials between coexisting phases.
Condition in which each microscopic transition is matched by its reverse transition.
Stable equilibrium condition for a closed system at fixed temperature and pressure.
State toward which a dynamical system returns after a sufficiently small disturbance.
Constant macroscopic condition maintained despite continuing internal or boundary fluxes.
Redistribution of heat until a common temperature is reached.
Progressive return toward a stable thermodynamic state.
Counteraction of deviations through a response that restores a reference condition.
Maintenance of temperature within a defined range.
Stabilization of temperature by absorbing or releasing latent heat near a transition point.
Coupling of a component to a controlled thermal reference or bath.
Measurement of absorbed energy through accumulated thermal response.
Restoration of equilibrium following a disturbance.
Maintenance of a subsystem near a prescribed temperature through a controlled reference.
Body large enough to absorb or release heat with minimal temperature change.
Controlled environment that establishes and maintains a reference temperature.
Structure that absorbs heat from a component to stabilize its operating temperature.
Chamber maintained at an approximately uniform temperature.
Measurement system designed to retain absorbed heat while minimizing environmental exchange.
Temperature-reference device maintained at a reproducible phase-transition condition.
Sealed reference system holding solid, liquid, and vapor in mutual equilibrium.
Detector that absorbs incident radiation and measures the resulting temperature change.
Conductive connection tying a subsystem to a stable reference temperature.
Internal heat transfer that reduces a temperature difference.
Capture of excess thermal energy by a stabilizing thermal mass or reservoir.
Uptake or release of transition energy to resist changes in temperature.
Absorption of energy into a measurement system for quantitative accounting.
Capture of radiation as measurable internal heat.
Conversion of an internal temperature state into a measurable physical signal.
Transfer of heat into a reference bath to preserve a controlled state.
Heat transfer across a sufficiently small temperature difference to approach equilibrium behavior.
Adjustment of heating or cooling within a closed control loop to suppress deviation from a reference state.
